title: What If the Oceans Were Fresh Water? The Fish Go First

scenes.text: What if every ocean turned to fresh water tonight? The fish would die before you could drink it.
Seawater holds about 35 grams of salt per litre. Marine fish drink it and pump the salt out through their gills.
In fresh water that machinery runs backwards. Most ocean fish can't switch, so most of them die.
Next, ice. Seawater freezes at minus 1.9 degrees, fresh water at zero, so polar seas ice over sooner and wider.
Then the currents. The ocean conveyor runs on cold, salty water sinking in the north. No salt, and that engine weakens.
Fresh oceans: dead fish, more ice, a colder Europe. The salt was doing more than you thought.

description:
What if the oceans were fresh water? Seawater holds about 35 grams of salt per litre; marine fish drink it and excrete the salt through their gills and urine, while freshwater fish do the opposite, and most bony fish cannot regulate in the opposite environment. Seawater freezes at about minus 1.9 degrees Celsius against zero for fresh water, so polar seas would freeze more readily; at least 15 percent of the ocean already carries sea ice for part of the year. The great ocean conveyor is driven by temperature and salinity, with cold, salty water sinking in the Norwegian Sea, and a weakened Atlantic circulation could mean colder temperatures in Europe.

first_comment: Sharks have their own trick: they keep urea in their blood to match the sea's saltiness. Which ocean animal do you think would adapt first?
